bibliographic.title: Methodological foundations of AI observability for enterprise LLM applications
bibliographic.venue: International Journal Of Engineering And Computer Science Volume 14 Issue 10
bibliographic.citation_apa: Gundu, V. (2025). Methodological foundations of AI observability for enterprise LLM applications. International Journal of Engineering and Computer Science, 14(10), 27748.

methodology.method_family: systems analysis, comparative analysis, conceptual architectural modeling
methodology.technology_context: enterprise LLM applications, LLMOps, conversational assistants, document analysis systems

eligibility.decision_rationale: The article explicitly targets methodological foundations of AI observability for enterprise LLM applications, proposing a multi-level framework across quality/semantics, cost/performance, security/privacy, and responsibility/ethics. It addresses LLM-specific risks (hallucinations, data leaks, cost escalation), couples automated metrics with human feedback, and discusses conversational assistants within enterprise deployment contexts relevant to governance and monitoring.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only partial full text was provided (pages 1-3 and fragments); peer-review status, complete framework details, methods rigor, and regulated-domain coverage require verification against the full article.

appraisal.notes: Conceptual/methodological study without empirical sample. Stated methods (systems analysis, comparative analysis, conceptual architectural modeling) fit the framework-building aim, but provided excerpts offer limited procedural detail on literature selection, comparative sources, or validation. Author acknowledges weak coverage of law, medicine, and finance.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are logically coherent and highly relevant to LLM observability and enterprise governance, but confidence is moderated because the work is conceptual, comparative-analysis procedures are not fully documented in the supplied text, and regulated-domain treatment is explicitly weak.

coding.theme: Methodological foundations of AI observability for enterprise LLMs
coding.subtheme: Multilevel observability framework spanning technical, economic, security, and ethical dimensions

synthesis.main_claim: Enterprise LLMs require a dedicated AI observability methodology beyond classical MLOps, operationalized through a multi-level framework that integrates automated metrics with human feedback across quality/semantics, cost/performance, security/privacy, and responsibility/ethics.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes a holistic conceptual methodology and reference architecture for designing LLM observability systems in corporate IT environments, systematizing dimensions and addressing LLM-specific risks not covered by traditional monitoring.
synthesis.limitations: Provided text indicates coverage of law, medicine, and finance is weak; full empirical validation, implementation evidence, and detailed comparative-analysis protocol are not evident in the supplied excerpts.
synthesis.use_in_review: Central evidence for the operational/technical governance strand on LLM observability, monitoring, logging/tracing-oriented governance, human feedback integration, and enterprise risk minimization; useful as a foundational framework paper rather than regulated-domain case evidence.
